title: Charlie Kirk's friend says preliminary hearing is about supporting family, seeking truth
text:
As prosecutors continued presenting evidence in the preliminary hearing for Tyler Robinson, the man accused of fatally shooting conservative commentator Charlie
Charlie Kirk's friend Jack Posobeic, of TPUSA, said the preliminary hearing is about supporting family and seeking the truth. As prosecutors continued presenting evidence in the preliminary hearing for Tyler Robinson, the man accused of fatally shooting conservative commentator Charlie Kirk, one of Kirk's closest friends said he came to Utah to stand beside the Kirk family.
Jack Posobiec, a conservative commentator who worked alongside Kirk at Turning Point USA, has attended the proceedings this week in Provo. He said he planned to travel to Utah even before learning Kirk's widow, Erika, and his parents would be in the courtroom.
"I was planning to be here even before we got the news that Erika had decided that she would come as well," Posobiec said. "Just to show support for Charlie and show support for this process, getting the information out, getting the facts out, getting the truth out. ""When I found out that Erika and Charlie's parents were going to be here, I said, well then, I absolutely have to come.
" The hearings have been emotional, he said, but he believes Kirk would have wanted the legal process to unfold properly. "It is grueling, obviously being in there in the courtroom day to day, and obviously it's very emotional for those of us who knew Charlie," Posobiec said. "But at the same time, I know that he would have wanted us to make sure that everything is done properly, that everything is done in an important manner.
"LIVE: Third day of preliminary hearing underway for man accused of killing Charlie Kirk "We're not going anywhere," he said. "Turning Point USA's mission will continue. Whether that means facing this, whether that means facing down whatever adversaries or challenges come our way, we are going to meet them.
""Charlie and I worked together every day, fought a lot of fights together, being in the trenches, politically speaking," he said. "We traveled around the country doing everything we could to fight for our beliefs and help put this country on a better track. ""That's what we talked about every day, and we prayed together a lot," Posobiec said.
"Charlie would have this thing where every morning he would actually text a Bible verse to the people he was close with, friends and family," Posobiec said. "We would just comment on that, and it was great because we would start every day with that. "Posobiec said he was preparing for his own show after Kirk's campus appearance at Utah Valley University. "It was the first campus stop of the tour, and so we were all excited," he said.
"School was getting back in session. Charlie was getting out there, and he had spent weeks preparing for this and had a binder full of different arguments and comebacks and all sorts of things he was researching.
""At first I thought maybe ... we get a lot of reports like that, and most of the time they actually turn out to be not true," Posobiec said. "Someone's trying to shut down an event, someone calls in a bomb threat, something like that. So my first thought was that I hope that's all it is.
""For some reason, this one felt different, even from the very start," he said. As reports began flooding in, Posobiec said he resisted saying anything publicly until he could verify the information.
"I said, 'Hey, I don't want to say this on air if it's not true. Can you contact somebody?
'" he recalled. "Work the phone chain to see if someone will answer so we can get some clarity of what happened. "Nearly 10 months later, Posobiec said he hopes the preliminary hearing helps establish the facts surrounding Kirk's death. He praised prosecutors for methodically presenting their case.
"I think the prosecution has been doing that," Posobiec said. "I think they've been methodical. I think they have been relentless.
" While acknowledging the pace has been slower than the world of news and politics, he said he understands why. "They are building the scaffolding of this case," he said. "We want the evidence to get out, number one, to make it clear what happened to Charlie, but number two, to make sure that people know why this happened and to understand what Charlie stood for.
""Charlie didn't stand for violence or hurting or pain or tearing people down," he said. "He wanted everyone to be able to build themselves up. He thought that embracing the Bible, embracing the teachings of Christ, that was the best way to live your life.
""From the youngest student or child all the way up to anybody who had come, that was Charlie," Posobiec said. "He did things the right way. He did things the peaceful way.
""It's surreal," Posobiec said. "It's quite a small room. Tyler's family is there, Charlie's family is there, and then Tyler's right there.
""It's a very, very big mix of emotions," he said. "There's moments of anger. There's moments of just feeling that chill down your spine, hair standing up on your neck.
" Robinson has pleaded not guilty to charges stemming from Kirk's death. Utah County prosecutors are seeking the death penalty. The preliminary hearing is expected to continue this week before a judge decides whether there is enough evidence for the case to proceed to trial.
